result.topic_en: Euler derives the differential equation between the coordinates of the elastic curve and begins classifying elastic curve species according to the sign and size of the coefficient 8n in the radical relating amplitude and radius of osculation.
result.transcription:
404 DE STATV AEQVILIBRII ET MOTV.
$\cos.\,\phi = \frac{dy}{ds}$ et $\sin.\,\phi = \frac{dx}{ds}$ erit $dy = dx \cot.\,\phi$,
vbi si loco $\cos.\,\phi$ valor substituatur orietur:
$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{aa - ax - nxx}{\sqrt{(2a^3x + (2n-1)aaxx - 2nax^3 - n^2x^4)}}$,
sicque inter coordinatas habebitur haec aequatio differentialis:
$dy = \frac{(aa - ax - nxx)\,dx}{\sqrt{(2a^3x + (2n-1)aaxx - 2nax^3 - n^2x^4)}}$,
XXXIII. Quo autem clarius intelligatur, quam variae curuarum species hic locum inuenire possint, consideretur illa aequatio inter amplitudinem $\phi$ et radium osculi $r$ inuenta:
$r = \frac{a}{\sqrt{(4n + 1 - 4n\cos.\,\phi)}}$,
vel quod eodem redit valor supra pro abscissa inuentus:
$x = \frac{a\sqrt{(4n+1-4n\cos\,\phi)}}{2n} - \frac{a}{2n}$, ita vt sit $x = \frac{aa}{2nr} - \frac{a}{2n}$,
quam eximiam proprietatem omnibus elasticis communem probe notari conuenit. Totum negotium ad formulam hanc irrationalem reducitur:
$\sqrt{(4n + 1 - 4n\cos.\,\phi)} = \sqrt{(1 + 8n\sin.\tfrac{1}{2}\phi^2)}$,
vbi imprimis spectandum est, an coëfficiens $8n$, sit positiuus an negatiuus, vel maior vel minor vnitate. Primum enim perspicuum est, si $8n$ fuerit numerus positiuus puta $= m$, tum formulam $\sqrt{(1 + m\sin.\tfrac{1}{2}\phi^2)}$ semper esse realem, ideoque angulum $\phi$ per omnes valores crescere posse; sin autem fiat $8n = 0$, elasticam fore circulum ob $r = a$. Si autem $8n$ fuerit numerus negatiuus, duos casus considerari oportet: alterum, quo vnitate fit minus, alterum, quo maius, priori casu quo $8n = -m$ et $m < 1$, formula

items.english: so that x = aa/(2nr) − a/(2n), a remarkable property common to all elastic curves which should be well noted.

items.quote: Quo autem clarius intelligatur, quam variae curuarum species hic locum inuenire possint, consideretur illa aequatio inter amplitudinem $\phi$ et radium osculi $r$ inuenta
items.english: To understand more clearly how various species of curves can occur here, consider the equation found between the amplitude φ and the radius of osculation r.

items.quote: si $8n$ fuerit numerus positiuus puta $= m$, tum formulam $\sqrt{(1 + m\sin.\tfrac{1}{2}\phi^2)}$ semper esse realem, ideoque angulum $\phi$ per omnes valores crescere posse
items.english: If 8n is a positive number, say m, then the formula √(1 + m sin²½φ) is always real, and hence the angle φ can increase through all values.

items.quote: sin autem fiat $8n = 0$, elasticam fore circulum ob $r = a$
items.english: If 8n = 0, the elastic curve will be a circle, since r = a.

items.quote: Si autem $8n$ fuerit numerus negatiuus, duos casus considerari oportet: alterum, quo vnitate fit minus, alterum, quo maius
items.english: If 8n is negative, two cases must be considered: one in which it is less than unity in magnitude, the other in which it is greater.
